output.name: Tanhá — the Gale's Tooth
output.myth: Tavo the Gale was out over the Windward cliffs in a fury, because a kite-line had gone stiff with salt and would not bend for him. He bit it hard, and his tooth came out in his jaw and went up. Tavo laughed, as he does. The tooth stuck in the Unflown, where things lost go, and has stayed there, white and cold, with the rope still in it. Kavesk the Cut End hangs under two fists west of it, a cord knotted to nothing, and has never said what it is missing. Varo the boatman sails by to the east, a shell coin on his palm. He will not stop for it; it has not drowned, so has no fare. Ennu the Kite-Wright says it could be fetched. Hesk says a counted thing cannot be uncounted. Aun, who would try anything, went south to fetch it. He came home with a bloody hand and no tooth, and said only that the tooth was smiling. So if you find yourself with a stiff line in a gale, do not bite it. Mend it with your hands.
output.finding: Sailors far south, past the last of the kelp, find Tanhá by starting at Varo, the Unpaid Crossing, and going one hand-span (about 20°) west along the same line to the cold white tooth, with Kavesk's cut cord a little under two fists beyond it.
